meta.title: Generic 1-6x24 second-focal-plane LPVO: optical system, eye box, reticle, zero tables and rendering model
meta.units: millimetres, degrees, MOA or mrad as each key says; SI in the zero tables; sockets in metres
meta.class_references: External figures of the class are in `published`. This is a generic scope: no maker's name, logo or trade dress; the optical design and the reticle are original.

published.doc: Published external figures of three 1-6x24 scopes, read on 2026-11-17. ft at 100 yd for the field of view.

vortex_razor_hd_gen2e.source: retailer technical specification page (scottcountry.co.uk, "Vortex Razor HD Gen II-E 1-6x24 Riflescope - Technical Specification")

trijicon_vcog.source: Trijicon VCOG spec sheet and product catalogue as summarised by a web search: field 95 to 15.9 ft, eye relief 4 in constant, exit pupil 0.41 to 0.15 in

sig_tango6t.source: SIG product page and a review (thefirearmblog.com, 2021) as summarised by a web search: field 105.8 to 17.7 ft, eye relief 3.9 to 4.1 in, exit pupil 11.4 to 4 mm

frames.asset: metres, +Z muzzle, +Y up, +X shooter's left; origin socket_mount = the rifle's socket_optic (rail top, on the centreline)
frames.shooter: eye offsets and field angles as the shooter sees them: right and up; right = -X of the asset frame

focal_plane_reason: Second focal plane. The reticle stays the same bold size at every power, so at 1x (where a carbine spends most of its time) the centre dot and ring are as quick as a red dot; a first-plane reticle fine enough to hold with at 6x shrinks to a speck at 1x. The cost: the BDC marks are true only at 6x. At another power every subtension is 6 / M times larger in object space (reticle_scale).

design.type: thin-lens (first-order) zoom: objective, field lens, two-group erector on cams, reticle-plane field lens, eyepiece
design.stop_model: From 6x down to 2.31x the objective rim is the aperture stop (exit pupil = 24 / M). Below that a stop in the erector cell, conjugate to the objective, holds the exit pupil at the ceiling.
design.note: A first-order design fitted to the published external figures of 1-6x24 scopes. It is not a lens prescription: aberrations come from the stated models, not from this layout. Its principal planes span 181.5 mm; the body is 257 mm long, because real groups are thick.

eyebox_function.doc: mask(ex, ey, dz, ax, ay) = overlap_area(disc(exit_pupil / 2), disc(eye_pupil / 2), separation) / (pi * min(r)^2), separation = hypot(ex + dz * ax, ey + dz * ay). ex, ey = eye offset from the axis (mm, right and up); dz = eye distance behind the exit pupil plane (mm, negative = too close); ax, ay = tangent of the apparent field angle of the pixel (right and up). Multiply by the vignetting profile and by image_brightness.
eyebox_function.eye_pupil_mm_from_luminance: d = 7.75 - 5.75 * f / (f + 2), f = (L * 2827 / 846)^0.41 (Stanley and Davies 1995, 60 degree field)
eyebox_function.behaviour: dz = 0: the whole picture dims evenly and then blacks out as the eye moves sideways. dz != 0: a crescent shadow enters from one side as the eye moves sideways and, with the eye centred, the field tunnels to tan(a) < (exit_pupil + eye_pupil) / (2 |dz|). Too far back, the shadow enters from the side the eye moved toward; too close, from the opposite side.

parallax.formula: error (rad, object space) = M * e * (1/D - 1/parallax_distance); e = eye offset in the exit pupil (m). The reticle appears to move over the target by this much.

distortion.model: r_d = r * (1 + k1 * r^2), r = field radius normalised to the field stop (r = 1 at the edge); positive = pincushion
distortion.source: inferred: typical edge distortion of 1-6x scopes (about 1 percent at 1x, 2 to 4 percent at 6x); a thin-lens model cannot predict it

transmission.source: inferred: about 90 percent for a fully multi-coated 1-6x; a slight warm cast is typical

illumination.what: centre dot only (an LED lights the etched dot), red 650 nm
illumination.off_appearance: the dot is etched, so it is black when the illumination is off
illumination.source: inferred: a "daylight bright" centre needs roughly 5e4 cd/m^2 to hold a Weber contrast of 3 on a sunlit paper target (20,000 cd/m^2)

turrets.elevation: top, capped, low profile; clips elevation_turn and elevation_cap_off
turrets.windage: right side, capped; clips windage_turn and windage_cap_off
turrets.illumination: left side knob, 11 positions; clip illumination
turrets.power_ring: half a turn from 1x to 6x with a throw lever; clip magnification (its angle is by_magnification[*].power_ring_deg)

design_eye_point: socket_eye is at the 6x exit pupil (the tightest eye box); the eye relief at other powers is listed per magnification

reticle.name: staple BDC
reticle.design: original (carpetshark): not a copy of any maker's reticle. The staple-shaped range marks carry two loads at once.
reticle.units: mrad at 6x; at magnification M every subtension is 6 / M times larger in object space
reticle.zero: 200 m on the centre dot, for either load (re-zero when the load changes: the two differ by 0.29 mrad of bore angle)
reticle.how_to_read: Centre dot: 200 m. Each staple below it is 300, 400, 500, 600 m (numbered). Hold the cross-bar on the target for M855, the tips of the legs for Mk 262. The bar is as wide as a 45 cm target at its distance, so it also ranges. The two small dots beside each bar are the hold for a 5 m/s full-value wind (M855).
reticle.ring_use: at 1x the ring is 15.6 mrad in radius: it frames a 45 cm wide target at 14 m and makes a fast close-range aiming circle

zero.convention: Distances are from the eye. bore_angle is the bore above the line of sight for an exact zero (POI = POA at the zero distance). clicks_up_from_centre is that angle in whole clicks from optical centre (line of sight parallel to the bore); the hold tables use the exact angle. poi_mm: + is high. hold: aim this much higher (+) to hit.

rendering.frame: Asset frame (metres, +Z muzzle, +Y up, +X shooter's left), origin socket_mount. The optical axis runs from socket_eye through socket_ocular_lens to socket_objective.
passes: 1. World pass: the normal scene camera at the shooter's eye.
2. Scope pass into a square render target: a camera at socket_objective looking along the optical axis, full field = real_fov_deg(M). Bias the scene level of detail as for a camera M times closer.

3. Composite on the ocular lens of the optic mesh (material lens_ocular) with the shader below. The body is ordinary opaque geometry, so the housing occludes the lens for free; that is what makes the picture move correctly with the eye.
rendering.render_target_px: 512 at 1x to 1024 at 6x is enough for a 1080p frame
shader: a = field direction of the pixel as seen from the eye: tangents (right, up) of the angle between the view ray and the optical axis. The image is at infinity, so it is fixed in angle while the housing slides over it; do not use the pixel's UV on the lens.
r = |a| / tan_half_apparent(M). If r > 1: black (field stop), with a 1.5 percent soft edge.
Distortion: r_src = r / (1 + k1 * r^2); uv = 0.5 + 0.5 * r_src * a / |a| (flip nothing: the erector makes the picture upright).
colour = render_target(uv) * transmission * vignette(r, M) * image_brightness(M, eye pupil).

Reticle: draw it in the same angle space, r scaled by reticle_scale(M) (second focal plane: constant on screen while the scene grows behind it). The etched layer multiplies toward black; the illuminated dot adds. Shift the reticle by M * parallax(e, D) if depth is available.

Eye box: colour *= mask(ex, ey, dz, a) from eyebox_function with exit_pupil(M) and the eye pupil for the scene luminance; dz = (eye distance behind the ocular lens) - eye_relief(M). This is the scope shadow.
Inside the lens but outside the image circle: black tube wall. Optional edge colour fringe: sample R and B at r * (1 -/+ 0.002 * r^2).

parameters.by_magnification: by_magnification[*]: tan_half_real, tan_half_apparent, exit_pupil_mm, eye_relief_mm, vignetting
parameters.vignette: interpolate vignetting.relative_illumination over field_fraction, then multiply by cos^4 of the apparent angle
parameters.both_eyes_open: at 1x the true magnification is 1.00, so the picture lines up with the world pass around the housing

rendering.runtime: OpticLPVO.state(M) and OpticLPVO.shade(state, eye, a) implement exactly these formulas; the sample page uses them per pixel.

parity_samples.doc: values for optic-lpvo.js to reproduce with its own cam solver, paraxial trace and mask
